memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, you are to offer a male without defect. You must present it at the entrance to the tent of meeting so that it will be acceptable to the LORD.'" - Lev 1:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two details stand out, and both matter.

First, without defect. Not the lame bull, not the sickly one, not the animal you were planning to lose anyway. God specified quality because worship reveals what we truly think of Him. Centuries later Malachi would rebuke Israel for bringing blind and crippled animals, asking whether they would dare offer such gifts to their governor (Mal 1:8).

Second, at the entrance. The worshipper could not choose his own place or his own terms. God set the meeting point. There is only one door.

Both details find their fulfilment in Jesus. Peter describes Him as a lamb without blemish or defect (1 Pet 1:19) — the only genuinely spotless offering ever made, because every animal before Him was at best a picture. And Jesus Himself said, "I am the gate" (Jn 10:9). He is both the perfect sacrifice and the appointed entrance.

This frees us from a heavy burden. You do not have to make yourself acceptable before you come. The burnt offering was accepted on the worshipper's behalf — the acceptability belonged to the offering, not the offerer. In Christ, God accepts you because of the spotless One who stands in your place.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I tempted to offer God what is convenient rather than what is worthy?
2. Do I try to make myself acceptable to God, or rest in the acceptability of Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I have nothing spotless to bring You except Your Son. Thank You that He is both my offering and my open door. Amen.
